title: In 210 worm mirror pairs, assigned active-zone volume varied less than a fixed-count random-size reference
abstract: We tested whether precise mirror synapse counts explain precise summed synapse volume in C. elegans. We used primary site annotations from six size-bearing brain maps and selected 210 mirror pairs with at least 16 pooled sites. The assigned active-zone volume difference score was 0.358. Keeping exact counts and randomly allocating the pooled measured sizes gave an exact expected score of 0.652. The mean paired difference was -0.294, with a crossed source-and-target class bootstrap interval of -0.397 to -0.169. One adult map gave a difference of -0.298, with interval -0.472 to -0.104. A whole-site sign reference retained shared polyadic targets. Size allocation structure remained with full active-zone volumes and at two other count cutoffs. These results extend count precision to a size-based anatomical weight under a stated random-size reference. They do not separate biological precision from shared annotation or geometric effects. Only one adult map had size data. The package contains new code, aggregate evidence, exact input hashes and a retrieval script. External record-level data remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Count and assigned-volume agreement, and volume agreement beyond the fixed-count random-size reference. Intervals resample neuron classes, not animals.

citations.reason: Extends the worm count result to primary site volumes and a fixed-count size reference.
